title: La Tomatina in Buñol, Spain: a 1945 street fight that became a yearly tomato festival, with a ban, a comeback, and a ticket limit

facts.text: La Tomatina takes place in Buñol, a small farming town in eastern Spain near Valencia.
Buñol has about 9,000 people.
The festival is held every year on the last Wednesday of August.
The tomato fight lasts about one hour.
The festival began by accident in August 1945, when young people broke into a parade in the town square and one of the boys grabbed a tomato, which started a tomato fight.

facts.text: The tomato fight was held again in later years until the early 1950s, when the Spanish ruler Francisco Franco banned it.
After local people protested the ban, officials allowed the festival again in 1957.
Television coverage later turned the festival into an event known around the world.
Before 2013 the festival could draw up to 40,000 people, and the crowd reached that size in 2012.
In 2013 the town charged a fee for the first time and cut the number of participants by half; the town hall said this was needed to limit the crowd for safety reasons.
Since 2013 La Tomatina has needed tickets and has been limited to about 20,000 people.
Today visitors who do not live in Buñol pay 15 euros for a ticket.
In recent years about 40 percent of the people taking part have been tourists from other countries.
Trucks bring the tomatoes into the crowd; more than 100 tons of overripe tomatoes are thrown each year, and up to 165 tons were used in 2026.
The main rule is that people must squash each tomato before throwing it, so that nobody gets hurt.
The fight may not start before a cannon is fired, and the sound of a cannon also marks its end.
After the fight, people wash off in public showers nearby and the streets are washed down with water.
The acid in the tomatoes helps clean the streets, which often end up cleaner than they were before the fight.
Some critics have said the festival wastes food while many people in the world do not have enough to eat.
The organizers say the tomatoes used are not good enough to be sold as food and would be thrown away anyway.
